Aisle Economics

Where does your food dollar go?

Click a glowing tag to see how much of each dollar reaches the farm — and how that shapes the way prices move.

The pattern

Groceries with a larger farm share transmit a change in farm-level costs to the shelf more directly. Items with a larger marketing share dilute that change — the effect is more likely to be delayed, muted, or filtered through processing, packaging, transportation, wholesale, retail, and other post-farm costs.

Aisle Economics

Where does your food dollar go?

Farm share helps explain price pass-through. When an item has a larger farm share, a change in farm-level costs is more visible in the retail price. When most of the price is marketing share — processing, packaging, transportation, wholesale, retail, and other post-farm costs — that change is more likely to be delayed, muted, or harder to see.

How to read each bar
Farm share
Marketing share
Farm share = cents that reach the farm. Marketing share = processing, packaging, transportation, wholesale, retail, and other post-farm costs. (Sample split shown.)
